confirmed_facts.fact: Laptop (LT-14, Electronics) delivered 2026-10-04; return requested 2026-11-03, 29.8 days after delivery, outside the 7-day electronics window.
Serial recorded at warehouse matches dispatch serial and the dispatch packing scan; the warehouse photo shows the same serial label.
Warehouse inspection found the unit does not power on, with no physical or liquid damage, and a bench test with a known-good charger failed.
Pickup weight 2.24 kg and received weight 2.23 kg are consistent; timeline is in order after UTC conversion.

findings.description: The return request is outside the 7-day electronics return window, so the standard return route is closed. The defect route is available because the fault is within 12 months of delivery and confirmed at inspection.

evidence.quote: Does not power on. No physical or liquid damage.

findings.description: Warehouse inspection records a non-powering unit with no physical or liquid damage and a note pointing to a board failure, consistent with a manufacturing defect for a person to confirm.

evidence.quote: Fault looks like a board failure
My laptop stopped turning on yesterday.

policy_references.quote: A manufacturing defect that appears within **12 months** of delivery is covered even after the return window has closed.
The defect must be confirmed by warehouse inspection or a technician report.

findings.rationale: The return is outside the 7-day electronics window under Return v2, but the warehouse inspection records a non-powering unit with no misuse damage, and the serial matches the dispatch record. Under the Defect policy, the remedy is repair or replacement arranged by the seller as a warranty case. A refund is offered only if neither is available within 14 days. A person should confirm.
findings.uncertainty_note: Only one policy version applies and the records agree. The inspection note says the fault 'looks like' a board failure, so a person should confirm it as a manufacturing defect.
